title: Installation methods
summary: Covers good practice for erecting wiring systems, including cable support, bending radii, MICC cables, caravans, drawing in cables and neat dressing.

sections.heading: Good practice in erection
paragraphs: The selection and erection of wiring systems must be in accordance with accepted good practice. There are regulations covering most areas and these must be complied with.

A common deviation from good practice is a lack of correct support for cables. Care should be taken when forming cables, because bending a conductor too tightly will damage the insulation and the conductor. See Appendix D of the On-Site Guide.
bullets: Follow accepted good practice and the regulations
Common deviation: lack of correct support for cables
Too tight a bend damages the insulation and the conductor
See Appendix D of the On-Site Guide

sections.heading: Installation methods and bending radii
paragraphs: BS 7671 chapter 52 gives more detailed information, and the system designer can also use manufacturer's guides. Sheathed and/or armoured cables in horizontal runs which are unlikely to be disturbed should be laid on a reasonably smooth surface. For inaccessible vertical runs, table D5 in the On-Site Guide should be followed.

Table D5, page 138 of the On-Site Guide gives details on bending radii. MICC cables may be bent to a radius not less than three times the cable diameter over the copper sheath, but only if the cable has not been reformed.
bullets: BS 7671 chapter 52 gives more detailed information
Horizontal runs unlikely to be disturbed: lay on a reasonably smooth surface
Inaccessible vertical runs: follow table D5 in the On-Site Guide
MICC: bend radius not less than 3 × cable diameter over the copper sheath
MICC bend allowed only if the cable has not been reformed

sections.heading: Particular applications
paragraphs: In caravans, sheathed cables in inaccessible spaces such as the ceiling need support at intervals not exceeding 0.4m for vertical runs and 0.25m for horizontal runs.

When drawing cables into wiring systems, take care not to exceed the system's maximum factor, found in Appendix E of the On-Site Guide. When drawing cables into trunking, support is required for vertical runs.
bullets: Caravans, inaccessible spaces: support at not more than 0.4m (vertical) and 0.25m (horizontal)
Drawing in: do not exceed the maximum factor in Appendix E of the On-Site Guide

sections.heading: Forming and dressing cables
paragraphs: Forming cables correctly ensures no damage occurs. Dressing cables neatly means future maintenance can be carried out. An untidy consumer unit may cause problems when circuits are to be identified.
bullets: Neat dressing: future maintenance can be carried out
Untidy consumer unit: circuits harder to identify
